transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-03 14:05 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Eric (Redwood SE), Diane (Willow MLOps), Ravi (Willow CTO), Sara (Willow Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in with Willow to review usage trends, discuss capacity bump for Q1, add eu-west region, and confirm security/KMS concerns. Agreement in principle to a 12-month renewal with a pilot of Dedicated capacity for one model family. Action items captured.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Diane: Diane here.
[00:08] Ravi: Ravi on the line.
[00:09] Sara: Sara here.
[00:11] Eric: Eric from Redwood, hi all.
[00:13] Maya: Great, so agenda — renewal terms, capacity bump, region add (eu-west), and any security questions. Would love to hear how usage has been since our last sync. Diane?
[00:28] Diane: Yeah, so overall things are good. We've seen about a 2.6x increase in token usage month-over-month as the recommendation engine rolled out to more customers. Peak windows are still around 11am PST for us, but the burstiness is higher. The dedicated pool you provisioned in July is hitting close to 80% most weekdays.
[00:46] Eric: When you say 80%, is that sustained or short spikes?
[00:50] Diane: Mostly sustained for 10-30 minute buckets, some longer on promo days. We're starting to see queuing for longer sequences which hurts p95.
[01:05] Ravi: Put bluntly, we want predictable latency for our users — p95 needs to be sub 350ms for most flows, otherwise the UX suffers.
[01:15] Maya: Totally. That's why we're here; to make sure renewal terms reflect projected capacity and to discuss adding eu-west to reduce regional latency for EU customers.
[01:27] Sara: On procurement, we need to understand commitment tiers for budgeting. Also, any new paperwork if we go dedicated for another model family?
[01:36] Eric: Not necessarily new paperwork — same contract addendum, but the dedicated pool sizing and SLA will be explicit. We can describe burst policies and autoscale behavior.
[01:46] Diane: Also KMS question — last time we tested KMS integration there were some failures during key rotation. That made us jittery. Will that change if we go Private or keep Hosted with VPC?
[01:58] Eric: Key rotation edge cases are usually network timeouts or IAM permissions. In Private deployments we can hand over KMS controls more directly; with Hosted we support customer-managed keys in several clouds — but we should run an integration test.
[02:15] Ravi: Our security team is clear: if we're extending to EU, data residency and audit logs must be in control. We need SOC2 evidence and access to audit streams.
[02:26] Maya: We can share the SOC 2 Type II pack; audit log streaming to your SIEM is possible via our console connectors. We'll note that for the tech call.

[02:40] Topics: Usage trends, dedicated capacity sizing, eu-west onboarding, KMS & audit logs, renewal discounting and PO timing.

[03:05] Maya: On pricing — given usage growth, are you leaning toward a fixed commit or a blended reserved + burst plan?
[03:12] Ravi: Ideally a commit that buys predictability for finance. But we want flexibility for seasonal spikes.
[03:18] Maya: We typically recommend a committed base for baseline traffic (e.g., X vGPU-hours / month) plus a burst buffer at a higher unit cost. That gives you an economic discount on the baseline but keeps room for spikes.
[03:32] Diane: Can you translate that to something concrete? Our baseline last quarter averaged 860 GPU-hours/week across the family. Projections put us at ~1.8k GPU-hours/week in Q1.
[03:45] Eric: Ok, so doubling — we should size a dedicated pool that covers your p95 during typical peaks with autoscale for heavier days. For EU, we'd replicate a smaller pool initially (say 20% of NA) and route EU traffic there.
[04:00] Ravi: And the SLA — p95 latencies? If we commit to dedicated pools, what's the guarantee?
[04:06] Eric: For Dedicated we back a latency SLO per route — we can craft a p95 SLO of 350ms for small-ish sequences. For long sequences, SLOs vary because of token-length economics. Also, fallback policies to other model variants can keep availability high.
[04:23] Sara: Procurement question — if we sign a 12-month commit, can we lock pricing for additional regions added later or do we get renegotiation?
[04:33] Maya: We can include a clause locking per-unit pricing for the commitment period for any identical capacity increments in other regions. However, changes in cloud costs or custom hardware may require negotiation — we'll try to be explicit in the quote.

[04:50] [05:00] Diane: One more operational note — our token distribution shifted: many prompts are now longer, so KV cache hit rate is down. We're worried that quantization or other perf knobs might change accuracy. Any guidance?
[05:17] Eric: We can run model-specific perf vs quality evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles; but we always recommend a holdback eval set to measure regressions. We'll attach a short eval template.
[05:34] Ravi: The other piece is routing policy — when eu-west goes live, can requests be regionally sticky? We don't want EU traffic jumping to NA and paying latency.
[05:45] Eric: Yes, routing policies support geo-sticky routing and failover chains — primary EU pool, secondary NA pool, and a fallback to a cheaper variant if both saturate.

[06:00] Maya: All right I'd like to propose terms in principle: 12-month renewal, committed baseline of 2,500 GPU-hours/week (across model families), dedicated EU seed pool at 20% capacity, and a 10% commit discount on baseline with burst at list price. Thoughts?
[06:20] Ravi: That sounds reasonable but need to validate budget. Can we see a folded pricing worksheet with an example monthly invoice?
[06:28] Maya: Yes — I'll draft a worksheet showing committed credit consumption, burst usage, and unit economics.
[06:33] Sara: Also include PO language: net-30 and our tax ID and payment instructions.
[06:38] Maya: Noted.

[06:45] [07:00] Diane: Quick tech clar — Eric, on the benchmark, can you include KV cache behavior with our typical prompt prefixes? That was the pain point last rollout.
[07:10] Eric: Yep, if you send the sample prompt set and a short runbook for simulated concurrency I can reproduce burst patterns. Preferably as a CSV or JSON.
[07:18] Diane: I'll upload to the shared folder.

[07:30] [07:45] Maya: Competitors — just to surface risk — are you still talking to Anthropic or any managed infra providers?
[07:52] Ravi: We had one exploratory with Anthropic on inference economics, and ManagedCloudAI ran a quick price comparison. Overall Redwood's feature set and rollout story are better, but pricing matters.
[08:05] Maya: Understood. We'll make sure the worksheet highlights unit cost at different utilization bands.

[08:15] [08:30] Eric: Security — KMS integration approach: for Hosted + CMK (customer managed key), we do envelope encryption and rotate keys with a test window. We'll run the rotation test in a staging window during the benchmark. If Willow opts for Private deployment later, you get full KMS control but different support/responsibility split.
[08:52] Ravi: Do you expose audit logs in near-real time? Our SIEM ingestion expects <5 minute lag.
[08:58] Eric: We have webhook/stream connectors and can confirm ingestion latencies; our typical lag is under 2 minutes if you use the pushed stream. We'll add that to the tech agenda.

[09:15] [09:30] Sara: Procurement timeline: if we sign intent by mid-November, can we have contracts finalized by end of November? Finance needs PO in December.
[09:41] Maya: That's feasible. We'll aim to send the first draft quote by 2025-11-07, and iterate quickly.

[10:00] Diane: Any limitations for the EU region around model variants or quantized runtime? We have specific privacy constraints for some models.
[10:12] Eric: Some hardware variants are only available in select regions. For EU we'll need to confirm hardware flavor (A100 vs H100 equivalent) and whether the quantized runtime we use is certified for your accuracy bar. We'll include a compatibility matrix.
[10:30] Ravi: Great. On SLA credits — how do they calculate for partial outages?
[10:37] Eric: SLA credits are pro-rated based on route-level SLO misses. We'll include the clause. For Dedicated we have stronger uptime guarantees and remediation timelines.

[11:00] Maya: Ok recapping: Maya sends quote + pricing worksheet by 2025-11-07. Eric runs a 48-hour benchmark and shares logs by 2025-11-10. Willow shares prompt set, GPU-hours numbers, and procurement timeline by 2025-11-10 to 11-12. We'll schedule the VPC/KMS deep dive for week of 2025-11-17.
[11:25] Sara: Sounds good. One small ask: can the renewal include an option to extend at the same committed rates for an added 6 months if usage grows faster? That would help budgeting.
[11:38] Maya: We can include an extension option with predefined rate bands; I'll add that as an optional clause.

[12:00] [12:15] Diane: Thanks everyone. Quick note — please flag any required network prep for VPC peering; our infra team needs a two-week lead.
[12:25] Eric: Will do — I'll add a short checklist in the tech deep dive invite.

[12:35] Ravi: If you can call out any caveats about model variant fallbacks (accuracy delta), that's helpful for our product managers.
[12:43] Eric: Yes, we'll include a delta table showing small token-level differences across quantized variants and the expected quality regression under heavy batching.

[13:00] Maya: All right, thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[13:05] Sara: Thanks.
[13:06] Diane: Thanks.
[13:07] Ravi: Good call.

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts ("KV cash", "peering timeout" misheard as "peer in timeout"), occasional speaker attribution errors near the start.

References/links mentioned: pricing worksheet (to be uploaded), SOC2 Type II pack (link provided post-call), staging prompt CSV (Willow -> shared folder), benchmark dashboard (Redwood will share).

End of transcript.
